title: Check yourself: Refining against an eval set, regression runs and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A new prompt raises the overall pass rate from 0.78 to 0.84. The per-item comparison shows that one input which passed before now fails. What should the team do?

options.text: Review that regression, then accept or repair it
options.says: The page says that "An average never excuses a regression": "If a case passed before and fails now, a person looks at it", and then the decision is made.

options.text: Ship it, because the pass rate rose
options.says: Ruled out because the example's v2 also raised the average and still failed its gate, and the rule for step 5 is to keep a change "only if every success dimension still holds and nothing regressed without a reason you accept".

options.text: Delete the failing item from the set, since it is noisy
options.says: Ruled out because "A case that disappears is not a pass", and dropping the case that fails "is the easiest way to improve a score".

options.text: Rerun the set until that input passes
options.says: Ruled out because a rerun until the input passes treats a signal as noise, while the page says "a flaky case is a finding".

origin.section: A run, a gate and a comparison

questions.stem: A regression run is scheduled for the day a team changes the model id in its configuration. Which failure does that run catch that a prompt-only check would not?

options.text: A prefilled assistant turn that the new release rejects
options.says: The page says a prefilled assistant message "returns a 400 on Claude 4.6 and later models", and that a regression run on the new id "turns each of those into a failed case the same afternoon".

options.text: A typo that crept into an example sentence in the prompt
options.says: Ruled out because an example sentence typo is a prompt edit, which the table already puts "Before the merge, as a check on the pull request".

options.text: An edit that fixes one case and breaks another
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives the prompt edit its own run, where "The edit fixes one case and breaks another", with no model id involved.

options.text: A label that was copied wrongly from a spreadsheet into the set
options.says: Ruled out because a wrongly copied label is a data error, and "The set lives in the repository beside the prompt", so a review of the diff finds it.

questions.stem: A team re-grades 800 items with a model every night, and nobody waits for the result. Which option cuts the price of that job the most while every item is still graded each night?

options.text: Grade a random tenth of the items each night
options.says: Ruled out because grading a sample drops cases, and "A case that disappears is not a pass".

options.text: Rerun the work on every commit instead of nightly
options.says: Ruled out because a run on every commit multiplies the requests, and the page says "A quick check on a pull request stays synchronous and small".

options.text: Submit the work through the Message Batches API
options.says: The page says the Message Batches API "charges half the standard price for work that can wait up to a day", and calls a nightly regression run "the typical batch job".

options.text: Send the items as parallel synchronous requests
options.says: Ruled out because the discount is for work that can wait, and synchronous calls take none of it: the Batches API "charges half the standard price for work that can wait up to a day".
